title: Bangsaen42 Marathon 2026 Review: Racing at Thailand's First Beach Resort
meta_description: Bangsaen42 Marathon 2026 review: November 15 at Bang Saen Beach -- Thailand's first government-built holiday resort, dating to 1943.
dek: Set for 15 November 2026 at Bang Saen Beach, this marathon runs along Thailand's oldest purpose-built holiday resort, established in 1943 and steeped in local folklore about two star-crossed lovers.
verdict: The Bangsaen42 Marathon runs along one of Thailand's most historically significant beach resorts -- Bang Saen, where the government built the country's first holiday resort in 1943. The beach's name itself carries genuine local folklore weight, tied to a tragic love story about two young Chonburi lovers whose names became attached to several nearby landmarks. Three distances (10K/21.1K/42.195K) put this squarely in serious-runner territory, without a shorter fun-run category. Organiser details weren't confirmed in research, and registration status is not yet announced.

sections.heading: Racing at Thailand's First Purpose-Built Resort
paragraphs: The Bangsaen42 Marathon offers three distances: 10K, 21.1K and the 42.195K full marathon, at Bang Saen Beach in Chonburi. [1] Bang Saen is genuinely historically significant: in 1943, the Thai government built the country's first purpose-built holiday resort there. [2] The beach itself stretches roughly 2.5km and sits about 108km east of Bangkok, close to both the capital and the larger resort city of Pattaya.

sections.heading: A Beach Named for a Tragic Love Story
paragraphs: The name Bang Saen comes from local folklore about two young Chonburi lovers, Saen and Sam Muk, whose unrequited love led them to throw themselves off a cliff together. [2] Their names became attached to several nearby Chonburi landmarks, including Khao Sam Muk, a low hill near the beach -- giving the race route genuine cultural texture beyond a generic coastal course.

sections.heading: Serious Distances Only
paragraphs: Unlike most races in this research batch, Bangsaen42 offers no category shorter than 10K -- the field spans 10K, 21.1K and the full marathon. [1] That focus signals an event aimed at committed distance runners rather than casual or family participants, similar to the Selangor Marathon's marathon-and-half-only format covered elsewhere in this research.
